care: This is reflective and spiritual work. It is not medical or psychological treatment and does not replace it. If you are struggling, please also reach out to a doctor or counsellor; in India, Tele-MANAS is free on 14416, day and night.

breath.care: Breathe gently and never strain. If you feel dizzy or uneasy, return to your normal breath. Skip the holds if you are pregnant or have a heart, blood-pressure or breathing condition, and ask your doctor if unsure.

soft.name: Long out-breath
soft.about: The simplest: a breath out that is a little longer than the breath in.

box.name: Box breathing
box.about: Four equal sides: in, hold, out, hold.

relax.name: 4-7-8, the relaxing breath
relax.about: Taught by Dr Andrew Weil: in through the nose for four, hold for seven, out through the mouth for eight. Four rounds is plenty to begin with.

sigh.name: Cyclic sighing
sigh.short: In · a little more · long out
sigh.about: A full breath in, a short second sip of air on top, then a long, slow breath out. In a 2023 Stanford study it lifted mood the most of the practices compared, at five minutes a day.

coherent.name: Coherent breathing
coherent.about: Even and unhurried: about six breaths a minute.

bhramari.name: Bhramari, the humming bee
bhramari.about: A pranayama: breathe in, then breathe out slowly with a soft, steady hum, the lips closed. Some cover the ears gently with the thumbs.
say: Hum softly as you breathe out

nadi.name: Nadi shodhana, alternate nostril
nadi.short: Left in · right out · right in · left out
nadi.about: A pranayama: rest the thumb on the right nostril and the ring finger on the left, and let the breath change sides. Without holds, which is how most begin.

body.hint: Tap a centre on the figure. These are the seven chakras of the modern system, shaped by John Woodroffe’s The Serpent Power (1919); older Indian traditions count and place them differently, and the rainbow colours were added in the twentieth century.

sahasrara.name: Sahasrara
sahasrara.place: at or just above the crown of the head

anahata.name: Anahata
anahata.place: at the centre of the chest

manipura.name: Manipura
manipura.place: at the navel, below the ribs

muladhara.name: Muladhara
muladhara.place: at the base of the spine

mend.start: Drag each piece home, or tap it
mend.note: Kintsugi is the Japanese art of mending broken pottery with lacquer dusted or mixed with powdered gold. The break is not hidden; it becomes part of the bowl’s history.

prompt.hint: Draft prompts; Sarvakali will write their own. Nothing here is saved.
prompts: What did I carry today that was never mine to carry?
Where in my body do I feel this, and what does it want me to know?
What would I say to myself at seven years old, if I could sit beside them today?
Which part of me did I hide this week, and what was it protecting?
What am I ready to set down?
What does rest honestly look like for me?
Who am I when no one is watching?
What did I dream, and how did I feel when I woke?
Where did I say yes when I meant no?
What small thing am I grateful for that I almost overlooked?

close.title: Healing begins with being heard
close.lede: Tell Sarvakali what you are carrying. Together you will find a gentle place to start.
